rationale: C21 is a clear drafting template for the child letter. Both are letters from Eisenhower to the territorial governor certifying the same procedural event under a statehood bill, followed by an almost verbatim sentence wishing the governor and territorial population well as they begin the process expected to culminate in admission as a State. The statutory section, territory, governor, and phrasing of the certification were adapted for Hawaii, while the distinctive structure and closing sentence were retained. C11 and C01 share statehood concepts but not this letter-specific machinery and language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In accordance with the provisions of Section 6 of Public Law 86-3, I am very happy to certify to you the fact that I approved the law today, March 18, 1959.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am happy to certify to you, as required by section 7 of H. R. 7999, that this measure was today signed into law.
shared_material.explanation: Both opening sentences certify presidential enactment pursuant to a specified section of the relevant statehood measure, with only Hawaii-specific statutory and date details substituted.

shared_material.child_excerpt: As you start the procedure that will, I hope, result in the admission of Hawaii into the Union as a State on equal footing with the other States, you and the people of Hawaii have my very best wishes.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: As you start the procedure that will, I hope, result in the admission of Alaska into the Union as a State, you and the people of Alaska have my very best wishes.
shared_material.explanation: This distinctive closing sentence is reproduced nearly verbatim, substituting Hawaii for Alaska and adding the equal-footing phrase.
